To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intraneuronal accumulation of PrP in sporadic C JD and E200K genetic Creutzfeld-Jakob disease is distinct in morphology and colocalization with early endosomal marker, and that the intraneurones of E200K genetic cases contain large inclusion body–like aggresome structures that are immunoreactive for PrP, ubiquitin, and p62.

the intraneuronic immunolabelling pattern for prion protein in E200K genetic Creutzfeld-Jakob disease differs from the pattern in sporadic Cretuzfeld-Jakob, and that the intraneuoronic immunolabellin pattern is associated with the presence of the E200K mutant prion protein in the brain.
intraneuronal immunoreactivity for the prion protein (prion protein immunoreactivity) in Creutzfeldt Jakob disease (CJ) is associated with the E2OK mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiological mechanisms of prion diseases, which can be caused by mutations in the prion gene (PRNP), by infection with prions or by spontaneous mutation.
the identification and characterization of intraneuronic prion protein (PRP) in sporadic Creutzfeld-Jakob disease and in E200K genetic Creutzfeld-Jacob disease.
the development of new methods of diagnosis, and the identification of the mechanisms that cause the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intraneuronic prion protein immunoreactivity in E200K genetic Creutzfeld Jakob disease is distinct from sporadic Creutzfeld Jakobs disease.

the presence of the E200K genetic mutation in the PRNP gene, which is responsible for the production of the mutant PrP protein, leads to the formation of the intraneuronic globular PrP deposits, which are not seen in the sporadic CJD cases.

the intraneuroneal prion protein immunoreactivity is not a feature of sporadic Creutzfeld-Jakob disease, but it is a feature of genetic Creutzfeld-Jacob disease, in particular the E200K genetic Creutzfeld- Jakob disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intraneuronal inclusions are not specific for any form of prion disease and are not pathognomonic for gCJD.
the intraneuroneal prion protein (prion protein, PrP) immunoreactive (ir) structures are a feature of genetic CJD associated with the E 200K mutation.
the E200K PrP is more toxic than the sporadic PrP, which explains why it can cause disease even in the absence of an infectious agent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of intraneuroneal PrP immunoreactive structures is associated with the E 200 K mutation and not with sporadic CJD, which may be of diagnostic value.
the E200K genetic form of CJD has unique pathological features that can be distinguished from other forms of CJD.

the intraneuritic PrP immunoreactive inclusions seen in sporadic and genetic CJD are different and that the E200K genetic cases have an additional type of intraneuritic inclusions that are not seen in sporadic cases.
